chapitres.desc: The pieces, capturing, checkmate and your first tactics.
Check and the ways out of it, castling, promotion, en passant, stalemate.

etapes.intro: When your king is attacked, it is in check, and you must deal with it at once. There are three ways: move the king, take the attacking piece, or put a piece in between.

exos.consigne: The rook is giving check and nothing can stop it. Move your king out of its line.
exos.apres: Out of check. Moving the king always works when a square is free.

exos.consigne: The bishop is giving check, and one of your pawns can take it. Take it.
exos.apres: The attacker is gone, and so is the check.

faux.*: That move does stop the check, but taking the bishop is even better: you win a piece.

exos.consigne: The bishop is giving check from far away. Push your pawn to the marked square, between the bishop and your king.
exos.apres: The pawn blocks the line, and your knight protects it. Blocking only works against a queen, a rook or a bishop: nothing blocks a knight.

faux.*: That gets out of check too. Here, try the third way: block with the pawn.

etapes.intro: Castling tucks your king away and brings a rook out, in a single move: the king goes two squares towards the rook, which jumps over it. Neither of them may have moved before, and nothing may stand between them.

exos.consigne: Castle on the short side: move your king two squares, to the marked square.
exos.apres: The king is safe behind its pawns, and the rook is ready to play.

faux.*: To castle, it is the king you move, two squares at once. Take it to the marked square.

exos.consigne: Now the long side: move your king two squares towards the other rook.
exos.apres: Same idea on the other side. One more rule: you can never castle while your king is in check.

faux.*: To castle, it is the king you move, two squares at once. Take it to the marked square.

exos.consigne: The black bishop watches a square your king would cross on the short side: castling there is not allowed. Castle on the other side.
exos.apres: The king never crosses an attacked square. The rook may: only the king's path counts.

faux.*: To castle, it is the king you move, two squares at once. Take it to the marked square.

etapes.intro: A pawn that reaches the last rank turns into another piece: you choose a queen, a rook, a bishop or a knight. Almost always the queen, the strongest of them.

exos.consigne: Push your pawn to the last rank and choose the queen.
exos.apres: A pawn has become a queen: that is how many games are won.

faux.e7e8r: That is allowed, but the queen is far stronger. Choose the queen.
faux.e7e8b: That is allowed, but the queen is far stronger. Choose the queen.
faux.e7e8n: That is allowed, but the queen is far stronger. Choose the queen.

exos.consigne: The knight blocks your pawn, but a pawn takes diagonally. Take the rook and choose the queen.
exos.apres: A capture and a promotion in the same move.

faux.b7a8r: That is allowed, but the queen is far stronger. Choose the queen.
faux.b7a8b: That is allowed, but the queen is far stronger. Choose the queen.
faux.b7a8n: That is allowed, but the queen is far stronger. Choose the queen.

exos.consigne: Checkmate in one move. Careful: this time the queen is not the right choice.
exos.apres: The knight gives check where a queen could not, and the king has no square left. It is rare, but it wins games.

faux.f7f8q: With a queen, the black king is not even in check. Try another piece.

etapes.intro: When a pawn moves two squares at once and lands right beside one of your pawns, you may take it as if it had moved only one square. This is en passant, and it is only allowed on the very next move.

exos.consigne: The black pawn has just moved two squares, right beside yours. Take it en passant: your pawn goes to the marked square.
exos.apres: The black pawn is gone, even though your pawn did not land on its square. It is the only capture in chess that works this way.

faux.*: That move is allowed, but we are after en passant: your pawn takes diagonally and lands behind the black pawn.

exos.consigne: Same thing on the other side. The black pawn has just jumped two squares: take it en passant.
exos.apres: Well taken. Remember: it is now or never, on the next move the right is gone.

faux.*: That move is allowed, but we are after en passant: your pawn takes diagonally and lands behind the black pawn.

exos.consigne: Two of your pawns can take it en passant. Pick one.
exos.apres: Either pawn would do: en passant belongs to any pawn standing right beside.

faux.*: That move is allowed, but we are after en passant: your pawn takes diagonally and lands behind the black pawn.

etapes.intro: If your opponent has no legal move left and their king is not in check, it is stalemate: the game is a draw, even if you are a queen up. Before you play, make sure they still have a move, or that you are giving checkmate.

exos.consigne: The black king has only one square left. Play any move that does not give stalemate: after your move, the black king must keep its square or be in check.
exos.apres: No stalemate: the black king still has a move, or it is in check. Six queen moves would have taken its last square without giving check.

faux.c5b6: Stalemate! The black king is not in check and has no move left: the game would be a draw.
faux.c5c7: Stalemate! The black king is not in check and has no move left: the game would be a draw.
faux.c5d6: Stalemate! The black king is not in check and has no move left: the game would be a draw.
faux.c5b5: Stalemate! The black king is not in check and has no move left: the game would be a draw.
faux.c5e5: Stalemate! The black king is not in check and has no move left: the game would be a draw.
faux.c5b4: Stalemate! The black king is not in check and has no move left: the game would be a draw.

exos.consigne: Same danger in the other corner. Find a move that does not give stalemate.
exos.apres: No stalemate. A game can also be drawn by agreement, or when the same position comes back three times.

faux.c6b7: Stalemate! The black king is not in check and has no move left: the game would be a draw.
faux.c6c7: Stalemate! The black king is not in check and has no move left: the game would be a draw.
faux.c6d7: Stalemate! The black king is not in check and has no move left: the game would be a draw.
faux.c6g6: Stalemate! The black king is not in check and has no move left: the game would be a draw.
faux.c6c2: Stalemate! The black king is not in check and has no move left: the game would be a draw.
faux.c6e4: Stalemate! The black king is not in check and has no move left: the game would be a draw.

exos.consigne: Your pawn is about to promote, but a queen would give stalemate. Choose the piece that avoids stalemate and still lets you give checkmate.
exos.apres: The rook left the king one square, then gave mate. Stalemate avoided.

faux.c7c8q: Stalemate! With a queen on that square, the black king has no move and is not in check.
faux.c7c8b: The bishop avoids stalemate. But a king and a bishop alone can never give checkmate: the game would be a draw as well.
faux.c7c8n: The knight avoids stalemate, and even gives check. But a king and a knight alone can never give checkmate: the game would be a draw as well.

etapes.titre: The boss: the computer without its queen
etapes.intro: You now know all the rules. To finish the chapter, beat the computer at its easiest level: it plays without its queen. No clock, and you can take a move back.

boss.gagne: Boss beaten. You know every rule of the game.

chapitres.desc: What each piece is worth, spotting what is hanging, saving an attacked piece, counting defenders, good trades.

etapes.intro: To tell whether a trade is good, players count in points: pawn 1, knight 3, bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9. The king has no price: lose it and you lose the game.

exos.consigne: Your queen can take two black pieces, and neither is defended. Take the one worth more.
exos.apres: Five points instead of three. When you have the choice, take the bigger piece.

faux.d1d5: The knight is worth 3 points, the rook 5. Take the rook.

exos.consigne: Your bishop can take a pawn or a knight, and neither is defended. Which one is worth more?

faux.d3f5: A pawn is worth 1 point, a knight 3. Take the knight.

etapes.intro: A piece is hanging when it can be taken for nothing: no one defends it. Before each move, look over your opponent's pieces: is one of them left unprotected?

exos.consigne: Your queen attacks three black pieces. Only one is not defended: take it.
exos.apres: A rook for nothing. That is what looking before you move pays.

faux.d1a4: The bishop is defended by a pawn: your queen would be taken back.
faux.d1d5: The knight is defended by a pawn: your queen would be taken back.

exos.consigne: Your knight attacks three black pieces. Only one is not defended: take it.

faux.e5d7: That piece is defended: you would give your knight in return. Look for the one nobody protects.
faux.e5g6: That piece is defended: you would give your knight in return. Look for the one nobody protects.

etapes.intro: When one of your pieces is attacked, you have four answers: move it away, take the attacker, put a piece in between, or defend it. Start with the first two: they are the safest.

exos.consigne: The black pawn attacks your knight. Move it to a square where nothing can take it.
exos.apres: The knight is safe. Before you settle on a square, check what the black pieces are watching.

faux.*: Your knight would be taken on the next move. Find it a square no black piece attacks.

exos.consigne: The black bishop attacks your rook. Simplest of all: take the bishop.
exos.apres: The danger is gone and you are a piece up.

faux.*: There is better: the bishop that attacks your rook is not defended. Take it.

exos.consigne: Your queen is under attack. Move her to a square where nothing can take her.
exos.apres: Safe. The more a piece is worth, the more carefully you look after it.

faux.*: Your queen would be lost. She is worth 9 points: find her a square no black piece attacks.

etapes.intro: A defended piece can still fall. Count your attackers and its defenders: with more attackers, and starting with your cheapest piece, you come out ahead.

exos.consigne: The black pawn in the centre is attacked twice and defended only once. Take it, starting with your cheapest piece.
exos.apres: Two attackers against one defender: the pawn is yours.

faux.d1d5: Start with the cheapest piece: if your rook takes first, you give a rook for a knight and a pawn, and lose on the deal.

exos.consigne: Two attackers, two defenders: taking now would cost you material. Bring a third attacker to the marked square.
exos.apres: Three attackers against two defenders: now the pawn is really in danger.

faux.c3d5: Two against two is not enough: after the trades, you come out behind.
faux.d2d5: Two against two is not enough: after the trades, you come out behind.

etapes.intro: To trade is to take a piece and be taken back. If you give less than you get, the trade is good: a knight (3) for a rook (5), for example. If you give more, keep your piece.

exos.consigne: Your bishop can take the rook. It will be taken back, but a rook is worth more than a bishop: make the trade.
exos.apres: You gave a bishop (3) and took a rook (5): two points gained.

exos.consigne: Your knight can take the rook, which the queen defends. Is it worth it? Count the points, then play.
exos.apres: Three points given, five taken. Players call this winning the exchange.

faux.*: The trade is worth it: a knight (3) for a rook (5). Take the rook.

exos.consigne: Your rook can take the knight, but it is defended: you would give 5 points for 3. Take the pawn nobody defends instead.
exos.apres: A pawn for free beats a losing trade.

faux.e4e7: The knight is defended by the rook: you would give 5 points to take 3.

etapes.titre: The boss: the computer without a rook
etapes.intro: Beat the computer at its easiest level: it starts a rook down. Keep your lead: give nothing away, and trade pieces whenever you can. No clock, and you can take a move back.

boss.gagne: Boss beaten. You know how to keep what you have.

chapitres.desc: The queen's kiss, the two-rook ladder, the back rank when it is guarded, the smothered mate.

etapes.intro: The queen mates on her own when she lands right next to the king and another piece protects her: the king cannot take her. Players call it the kiss of death.

exos.consigne: Mate in one: put your queen right next to the black king, on a square your pawn protects.
exos.apres: Mate. The king cannot take the queen: your pawn protects her.

exos.consigne: Mate in one. This time, your knight protects the queen.
exos.apres: The knight holds the queen, and the king's own rook and pawns block the rest: mate.

exos.consigne: Mate in one. Your bishop is hiding behind your queen: it will protect her all along the diagonal.
exos.apres: Queen and bishop on the same diagonal: when the queen moves up, the bishop protects her from afar. Both mates worked.

etapes.intro: Two rooks can mate without help from the king. One guards a rank, the other gives check on the next one, then they swap roles. Each time, the king steps back one rank, until it reaches the edge.

exos.consigne: The king is on the edge. One of your rooks guards the rank just in front of it. Mate with the other one.
exos.apres: One rook gives check, the other shuts the way out: mate.

exos.consigne: Same idea, on the side of the board. One rook guards the file next to the king. Mate with the other one.
exos.apres: The ladder works both ways, along ranks or along files.

exos.consigne: The black king is still far from the edge. One rook guards the rank below it. With the other, give check on the marked square to push it back.
exos.apres: The king steps back, then the other rook takes its turn. Two more checks and it is mate.

etapes.intro: You know the back-rank mate: a king shut in behind its pawns, a rook on its last rank. It fails if a piece guards that rank. And it can hit you too: a pawn pushed in front of your king gives it a square to escape.

exos.consigne: Mate in one on the last rank. Careful: the black bishop guards one of the two squares.
exos.apres: Before playing the back-rank mate, check that nothing guards the square.

faux.d1d8: The black bishop guards that square: it would take your rook, and there would be no mate.

exos.consigne: The black rook threatens mate on your last rank. Push one of the pawns in front of your king by one square: it will have a square to escape.
exos.apres: Your king now has an escape square: the back-rank mate no longer works. Players often make this small pawn move when they have time.

faux.*: Push one of the three pawns in front of your king by one square: it will have a square to escape.

etapes.intro: When the king is surrounded by its own pieces, it has no square left. Nothing can be put in the way of a knight's check: this is the smothered mate.

exos.consigne: The black king is stuck in its corner by its rook and pawns. Mate with your knight.
exos.apres: The king is smothered by its own pieces, and nothing can take the knight.

exos.consigne: Same thing in the other corner. Find the square from which your knight mates.
exos.apres: Smothered mate. It is rare, but when it comes, the king has no answer.

etapes.intro: Before taking a piece, even the queen, look at all your checks. Checkmate ends the game: it is worth more than any capture.

exos.consigne: Your knight can take the black queen. But look at your checks first: there is better.
exos.apres: Mate. The black queen did not matter any more.

faux.e5c6: Winning the queen is good, but you had mate in one. Always look at your checks first.

exos.consigne: Your rook can take the black queen. Before you do, look at your checks.
exos.apres: Back-rank mate. The king first, the pieces after.

faux.b1b3: Winning the queen is good, but you had mate in one. Always look at your checks first.

etapes.titre: The boss: the computer without a knight
etapes.intro: Beat the computer at its easiest level: it starts a knight down. Look for the mates of this chapter: the back rank, the queen's kiss, the two rooks. No clock, and you can take back a move.

boss.gagne: Boss beaten. You know the mates that come up most often.

chapitres.desc: Attacking two things at once: with a knight, a pawn, the queen, a check, or a piece that steps aside.

etapes.intro: You saw the fork in chapter 1. It is even stronger with a check: the king has to move, and the knight takes the other piece. Look for the squares from which your knight hits the king and a big piece.

exos.consigne: Find the knight move that gives check and attacks the rook at the same time.
exos.apres: The king has to move, and the rook falls.

exos.consigne: This time your knight can hit the king and the queen. Find the square.
exos.apres: A queen for nothing: the best fork of all.

exos.consigne: Find the knight check that also attacks the rook.
exos.apres: You now have a knight and a pawn against a lone king.

etapes.intro: The smallest piece can also attack two at once: a pawn captures diagonally, to the left and to the right. It is worth only 1 point, so losing a piece to it costs a lot.

exos.consigne: Push your pawn between the two knights: it will attack both.
exos.apres: One knight runs away, the pawn takes the other.

exos.consigne: Find the pawn move that attacks the bishop and the knight. If the bishop takes it, your other pawn takes back.
exos.apres: A pawn is worth 1 point, a bishop 3: the pawn won.

etapes.intro: The queen moves in every direction: from a single square, she can aim at two pieces that are not defended. Your opponent can save only one.

exos.consigne: The black knight and bishop are not defended. Find a square from which your queen attacks both, where nothing can take her.
exos.apres: Black cannot save everything: you will win a piece.

faux.e3g5: Your queen attacks both pieces from there, but the black pawn would take her.

exos.consigne: Give check with your queen while also attacking the knight.
exos.apres: The king has to get out of check, and the knight falls.

etapes.intro: A check forces your opponent to deal with the king. If the same piece also attacks another piece, that piece falls on the next move. With a rook, look for a line that runs through the king and an undefended piece.

exos.consigne: Give check with your rook on the king's rank: it will attack the knight as well.
exos.apres: The king steps aside, the rook takes the knight.

exos.consigne: Give check with your rook on the king's file, right in front of it: your king protects it, and it attacks the bishop.
exos.apres: The rook cannot be taken, the king has to move, and the bishop falls.

etapes.intro: When a piece steps aside, it can unmask another piece hidden behind it. If the piece that moves gives check, your opponent has no time to save what is attacked behind.

exos.consigne: Your bishop hides your rook, which aims at the black queen. Move the bishop away with check.
exos.apres: The king has to answer the check, and your rook takes the queen.

exos.consigne: Your knight hides your bishop, which aims at the black king. Move the knight away to give check with the bishop, onto a square where it also attacks the queen.
exos.apres: Black has to deal with the king, and the queen falls.

etapes.titre: The boss: the computer without a bishop
etapes.intro: Beat the computer at its easiest level: it starts a bishop down. On every move, look for a piece of yours that could attack two at once. No clock, and you can take back a move.

boss.gagne: Boss beaten. You know how to attack two pieces at once.

chapitres.desc: The pinned piece, which cannot or should not move, and the skewer, which wins the piece behind.

etapes.intro: A piece pinned to its king is not allowed to move: it would leave the king in check. That makes it an easy target: attack it, with a pawn if you can, and it falls.

exos.consigne: Your bishop pins the black knight to its king. Attack the knight with a pawn.
exos.apres: The knight cannot run away: it falls to a simple pawn.

exos.consigne: Your rook pins the black knight to its king. Attack it with a pawn.
exos.apres: Same idea with a rook: the pinned piece is lost.

etapes.titre: A pinned piece no longer defends
etapes.intro: A piece pinned to its king cannot take back: that would leave the king in check. So what it seems to defend is not really defended.

exos.consigne: The black knight is defended only by a pawn, and your rook pins that pawn. Take the knight.
exos.apres: Check, and the pawn cannot take back: it is pinned.

exos.consigne: The black knight is defended only by a pawn, which your rook pins on the king's file. Take the knight.
exos.apres: The pawn cannot take back without leaving its king in check.

etapes.intro: A piece can also be pinned to its queen. Then it is allowed to move, but the queen behind it would be taken. So it stays put, and becomes a target.

exos.consigne: Pin the black knight to its queen: put your bishop on the marked square.
exos.apres: If the knight moves, your bishop takes the queen.

exos.consigne: The black bishop is defended only by the knight, and the knight is pinned to its queen. Take the knight.
exos.apres: The defender is gone: when the queen takes back, your rook takes the bishop.

etapes.intro: A skewer is a pin turned around: the big piece is in front. You attack it, it has to step aside, and you take the piece behind. With a check, it works every time.

exos.consigne: Give check with your rook on the king's rank: the queen is behind it.
exos.apres: The king steps aside, and the queen falls.

exos.consigne: Same idea with the black rook: give check on the king's rank.
exos.apres: The black rook was behind its king: it is lost.

etapes.intro: When something holds only thanks to one defender, deal with the defender first: take it, or chase it away. What it was protecting falls next.

exos.consigne: Your queen and bishop aim at the square next to the black king. Only the knight stops your queen from mating there: take it with your rook.
exos.apres: The defender is gone. If the pawn takes back, your queen mates next to the king, protected by your bishop.

exos.consigne: Same picture, but this time chase the knight away with a pawn.
exos.apres: Chased away, the knight no longer stops the mate: your queen mates next to the king.

etapes.titre: The boss: the computer two pawns down
etapes.intro: Beat the computer at its easiest level: it starts two pawns down. Look for pieces lined up with its king or queen: a pin or a skewer may be waiting. No clock, and you can take back a move.

boss.gagne: Boss beaten. You know how to pin and skewer.

chapitres.desc: The three ideas of the first moves: take the centre, bring out your pieces, put your king in safety. And the traps to avoid.

etapes.intro: The four squares in the middle matter most: a piece in the centre can go everywhere. Start by moving a pawn there, two squares forward.

exos.consigne: Move one of the two centre pawns two squares forward.
exos.apres: Your pawn holds the centre and opens the way for your queen and a bishop.

faux.*: To start, move the pawn in front of your king or your queen two squares forward.

exos.consigne: Black moved their pawn only one square. Move your other centre pawn two squares forward.
exos.apres: Two pawns in the centre: your pieces will have room.

faux.*: Move the pawn in front of your queen two squares forward, next to your first pawn.

etapes.intro: Next, bring out your knights and bishops, towards the centre. A piece on the edge of the board controls fewer squares. Early on, avoid moving the same piece twice.

exos.consigne: Bring out a knight towards the centre.
exos.apres: The knight points at the centre.

faux.*: Bring out a knight, towards the centre rather than the edge.

exos.consigne: Bring out your bishop to a square from which it aims at the f7 pawn, Black's weak spot.
exos.apres: The f7 pawn is defended only by the king: your bishop is already watching it.

faux.*: Look for the square from which your bishop sees the f7 pawn, along a diagonal.

etapes.intro: Bringing your queen out straight away is tempting, but she gets chased. Each time you attack her while bringing out a piece, you gain time.

exos.consigne: The black queen came out very early. Bring out a knight that attacks her.
exos.apres: The queen has to run, and your knight came out at the same time.

faux.*: Find the knight move that attacks the black queen.

exos.consigne: Another queen out too early. Bring out a piece that attacks her.
exos.apres: The queen has to move again while your pieces come out.

faux.*: Attack the queen with a piece you bring out, not with a pawn.

etapes.intro: Once your knight and bishop on the king's side are out, castle. Your king hides behind its pawns, and your rook joins the game.

exos.consigne: Your knight and bishop are out. Put your king in safety by castling.
exos.apres: Your king is safe, and your rook is ready to play.

faux.*: To castle, move your king two squares, onto the marked square.

exos.consigne: The black knight and bishop aim at your f2 pawn. Castle: your rook will come and defend it.
exos.apres: The f2 pawn is now defended by your king and your rook.

faux.*: To castle, move your king two squares, onto the marked square.

etapes.intro: A queen and a bishop aiming together at the f2 or f7 pawn can mate in four moves: this is the Scholar's mate. Know it, so you can stop it, and use it if your opponent forgets.

exos.consigne: The black queen and bishop aim at your f2 pawn: they threaten mate. Protect that pawn, or chase the queen away with a pawn.
exos.apres: The f2 pawn is safe. In your games, always keep an eye on it: early on, only your king defends it.

faux.g1f3: The knight attacks the queen, but it does not protect f2: the queen would mate there.
faux.e1e2: Your king does protect the pawn, but it can no longer castle and stays exposed in the centre.
faux.*: This move neither protects the f2 pawn nor chases the queen with a pawn.

exos.consigne: Black forgot to protect f7. Your queen and bishop aim at it: mate.
exos.apres: The Scholar's mate. It works only if your opponent does not see the threat.

etapes.intro: This time, no handicap: beat the computer at its easiest level, on equal terms. Take the centre, bring out your pieces, castle. No clock, and you can take back a move.

boss.gagne: Boss beaten. You know how to start a game well.

chapitres.desc: Mating with the queen, then with the rook, and taking a pawn all the way to promotion.

etapes.intro: With a queen and your king against a lone king, you win: push the king to the edge, then your king helps the queen to mate. The danger is stalemate: always leave the other king a move until you mate.

exos.consigne: Mate in one. Careful: two queen moves give stalemate.
exos.apres: Mate. Your king guards the squares in front of the black king, the queen closes the edge.

faux.f1c4: Stalemate! The black king is not in check and has no move left: the game would be a draw.
faux.f1f7: Stalemate! The black king is not in check and has no move left: the game would be a draw.

exos.consigne: Same thing in the other corner: mate, without stalemate.
exos.apres: Mate. Remember the picture: your king close by, the queen on the edge rank.

faux.c1c7: Stalemate! The black king is not in check and has no move left: the game would be a draw.
faux.c1f4: Stalemate! The black king is not in check and has no move left: the game would be a draw.

etapes.intro: With a rook it takes longer, but the idea is the same. The mate happens on the edge: your king stands opposite the other king, one square between them, and the rook gives check along the edge.

exos.consigne: The two kings face each other. Mate with your rook.
exos.apres: Your king guards the three squares in front of the black king, the rook holds the edge: mate.

exos.consigne: Mate in one. Careful: one rook move gives stalemate.
exos.apres: Mate. Here the kings do not face each other, but the black king is in the corner: it works too.

faux.a7g7: Stalemate! The black king is not in check and has no move left: the game would be a draw.

etapes.intro: Can a lone pawn escape the other king? Picture a square from the pawn to its promotion square. If the king can step into that square, it catches the pawn. If not, the pawn becomes a queen.

exos.consigne: The black king is far away. Push your pawn: the king will not be able to catch it.
exos.apres: The black king is outside the square: your pawn will become a queen.

exos.consigne: The black pawn is running to your first rank. Step your king into its square to catch it.
exos.apres: Your king is inside the square: the pawn will not get through.

etapes.intro: When two kings face each other with one square between them, the side to move has to give way. The other side is said to have the opposition. In pawn endgames, it often decides everything.

exos.consigne: Take the opposition: put your king right opposite the black king, with one square between them.
exos.apres: Black is to move: their king has to step aside, and yours moves forward.

faux.*: Put your king on the marked square, opposite the black king.

exos.consigne: The kings face each other, but it is your move. Your pawn can take a small step: move it one square.
exos.apres: Now Black is to move with the kings facing each other: they have to give way.

faux.*: Move your pawn just one square: then Black has to move instead of you.

etapes.titre: The king in front of its pawn
etapes.intro: To take a pawn to promotion, the king goes in front of it and clears the way. A pawn pushed too soon gets stopped; a well-placed king escorts it to the end.

exos.consigne: Your pawn is blocked by your own king. Move your king one rank forward, towards the black king.
exos.apres: Your king gains ground in front of the pawn: the way is opening.

exos.consigne: Your king is in front of its pawn, facing the black king. Move it to the side, without stepping back, to keep the squares in front of the pawn.
exos.apres: The black king cannot block the pawn: it will become a queen.

etapes.titre: The boss: king and queen against a lone king
etapes.intro: To finish the chapter, mate with your king and queen against the computer's lone king, which defends as well as it can. Push its king to the edge, bring yours closer, and watch out for stalemate. You have 50 moves. You can take back a move.

boss.gagne: Boss beaten. You know how to mate with the queen.

chapitres.desc: A first move that forces everything, then the mate. This time, you play both moves.

etapes.intro: In a mate in two, your first move leaves your opponent no choice, then your second move mates. The simplest way: a first check that drives the king to the edge, a second one that mates it.

exos.consigne: Mate in two. Start with a check that pushes the king back to the last rank.
exos.ensuite: The king stepped back. Now mate.
exos.apres: One rook closes a rank, the other mates: the two-rook ladder, in two moves.

exos.consigne: Mate in two. Your rook gives check first, your queen finishes the job.
exos.apres: The rook holds one rank, the queen mates on the next.

etapes.intro: Sometimes the first move gives a piece away. Here the queen sacrifices herself: the black rook has to take her, and your rook takes back with mate on the last rank.

exos.consigne: Mate in two. Your queen and rook are on the same file. Give up your queen with check.
exos.ensuite: The black rook took your queen. Take back with mate.
exos.apres: A queen given for mate: the best trade there is.

exos.consigne: Same idea on the other side: mate in two.
exos.apres: The black king is shut in behind its pawns: the last rank is fatal.

etapes.intro: You know the smothered mate from chapter 4. To set it up, your queen sacrifices herself right next to the king: the black rook has to take her and blocks the king's last square. Then the knight mates.

exos.consigne: Mate in two, with a queen sacrifice and a smothered mate. Your knight protects the square next to the king.
exos.ensuite: The rook took your queen and walled in its king. Mate with your knight.
exos.apres: The smothered mate: the king is walled in by its own pieces.

exos.consigne: Same thing in the other corner: mate in two.
exos.apres: Smothered mate. The queen sacrifice was worth it.

etapes.intro: The first move is not always a check. Here your king comes closer and takes away every square from the black king but one. It has a single move left, and then it is mate.

exos.consigne: Mate in two. Start with a king move that leaves the black king a single square.
exos.ensuite: The black king had only one square. Now mate.
exos.apres: Your king closed the squares, your rook mated.

exos.consigne: Same idea with the queen: bring your king closer so the black king has only one square left.
exos.apres: Your queen mates while your king guards the squares.

etapes.intro: The strongest move is sometimes a calm one: no check, no capture. It leaves the black king a single move, and that move leads to mate.

exos.consigne: Mate in two. The first move does not give check: it shuts the black king in.
exos.apres: A calm move, then mate: the black king had no way out.

exos.consigne: Another quiet move: mate in two.
exos.apres: Your queen cut the king off, your king guarded the squares next to it: mate.

etapes.intro: The last boss of the path: the computer plays one level stronger, but starts a knight down. Look at checks, captures and threats, and watch for a mate in two. No clock, and you can take back a move.

boss.gagne: Boss beaten. You have finished the path: you have all the basics.

placement.ex: The knight on b7 was not defended: the bishop takes it for free.
The queen goes right next to the king, protected by your own king: checkmate.
The king is shut in behind its pawns: the rook mates on the last rank.
The pawn that just moved two squares attacked your bishop and your knight. Taking it en passant removes it, and your knight protects your pawn.
Promoting to a knight gives check, and the king has no square left: checkmate. A queen would not even have given check.
Of the three pieces your queen attacked, only the rook was not defended.
The pawn was attacked twice and defended only once. Taking with the knight first wins it.
One rook closes the rank in front of the king, the other gives check on the edge: mate. This is the two-rook ladder.
The knight gives check and the king is shut in by its own rook and pawns: smothered mate.
The knight gives check and attacks the queen at the same time: a fork. The king must move, and the queen falls.
The queen gives check on the king's file and attacks the knight along the diagonal: the king moves, the knight falls.
The bishop attacks the queen, which cannot step aside: her king is right behind her. This is a pin, and the queen is lost.
The rook gives check on the king's file, and the black rook is behind it: the king steps aside, the rook falls. That is a skewer.
Black moved the two pawns in front of their king: the queen mates on the diagonal that is now open.
The f7 pawn was defended only by the king, and your bishop protects the queen: the Scholar's mate.
The black king is outside the square of the pawn: once it moves forward, nothing can catch it.
The kings face each other: your king guards the squares in front, and the rook mates along the edge.
The queen gives herself up on the last rank: the rook must take her, and your rook takes back with checkmate.
The queen gives check and shuts the king in with your rook: whatever it plays, mate follows on the next move.
